announcements.text: The Boeing Co., St. Louis, Missouri, is being awarded $109,027,999 for ceiling-price delivery order (N00383-26-F-YY29) under a previously awarded basic ordering agreement (N00383-22-G-YY01) for the procurement of 76 outer wing panels utilized on the F/A-18 aircraft. The delivery order does not include an option provision. Work will be performed in St. Louis, Missouri (90%); and Hazelwood, Missouri (10%). Work is expected to be completed by October 2031. Fiscal 2026 working capital funds (Navy) in the amount of $53,423,719 (49%) will be obligated at the time of award and funds will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. An additional $55,604,280 remains committed to fund the ceiling-priced delivery order that has a maximum total value of $109,027,999. One source was solicited for this sole-source requirement pursuant to the authority set forth in 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1) and one offer was received. Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon Systems Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity.

Supply Chain Management Inc.1.com (SCMI1),* Hauppauge, New York, was awarded a $20,766,943 firm-fixed-priced contract action, for providing various technical and logistical services to Navy surface combat weapons systems, with maintenance, and training associated with the installation, operation, alteration, and readiness of shipboard equipment and services. Work will be performed in Jacksonville, Florida, and is expected to be completed by August 2027. This contract contains options, which if exercised, would bring the cumulative value to $20,766,943, and would extend the period of performance to August 2032. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance (Navy) funding in the amount of $3,775,808 were obligated at the time of award, of which, funds in the amount of $3,775,808 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured using full and open competition via the System for Award Management website with four offers received. Southeast Regional Maintenance Center, Mayport, Florida, is the contracting activity (N40027-26-F-3002). (Awarded Aug. 7, 2026).

Systems Application & Technologies Inc.,* Upper Marlboro, Maryland, is awarded a $20,748,572 cost-plus-fixed-fee contract. This contract provides technical, engineering, supply, administrative, program analysis and management, and facility contractor support services for the Aircraft Instrumentation Division. These services support the design, development, procurement, building, installation, testing and evaluation, calibration, modification, operation, and maintenance of instrumentation on aircraft and uninstalled engines for the Navy, other government, commercial, and foreign government customers. Work will be performed in Patuxent River, Maryland (98%); and various locations within the continental U.S. (2%), and is expected to be completed in September 2027. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $4,000 will be obligated at time of award. This contract was competitively procured as a small business set-aside via an electronic request for proposal; six offers were received. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity (N0042126C0030).

Childs Engineering Corp.*, Bellingham, Massachusetts, was awarded a firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for architect-engineering services for routine inspection of waterfront facilities. Work will be performed in the U.S. in the Northeast, Southeast, Great Lakes area, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands, and is expected to be completed by August 2031. The maximum dollar value, including the base period, is $15,000,000. Fiscal 2026 Navy Working Capital funds in the amount of $10,000 will be obligated at time of award to satisfy the minimum guarantee, and funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with four offers received. Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center, Port Hueneme, California, is the contracting activity (N39430-26-D-4001).

Appledore Marine Engineering,* LLC, Portsmouth, New Hampshire, was awarded a firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for architect-engineering services for routine inspection of waterfront facilities. Work will be performed within the U.S. in the Mid-Atlantic region, Virginia, Maryland, and Washington D.C., and is expected to be completed by August 2031. The maximum dollar value, including the base period, is $15,000,000. Fiscal 2026 Navy Working Capital funds in the amount of $10,000 will be obligated at time of award to satisfy the minimum guarantee, and funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with four offers received. Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center, Port Hueneme, California, is the contracting activity (N39430-26-D-4002).

Engineering Operations LLC,* Littleton, Colorado, was awarded a firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for architect-engineering services for routine inspection of waterfront facilities. Work will be performed within the continental U.S. in the Southwest, Hawaii, and Gulf Coast areas, and is expected to be completed by August 2031. The maximum dollar value, including the base period, is $15,000,000. Fiscal 2026 Navy Working Capital funds in the amount of $10,000 will be obligated at time of award to satisfy the minimum guarantee, and funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with four offers received. Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center, Port Hueneme, California, is the contracting activity (N39430-26-D-4003).

Appledore Marine Engineering,* LLC, Portsmouth, New Hampshire, was awarded a firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for architect-engineering services for routine inspection of waterfront facilities. Work will be performed within the U.S. Northwest region and Alaska and at outlying areas including, but not exclusive of, American Samoa, Federated States of Micronesia, Guam, Midway Island, Wake Island, Johnson Atoll, Baker Island, and the Northern Mariana Islands, and is expected to be completed by August 2031. The maximum dollar value, including the base period, is $15,000,000. Fiscal 2026 Navy Working Capital funds in the amount of $10,000 will be obligated at time of award to satisfy the minimum guarantee, and funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with four offers received. Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center, Port Hueneme, California, is the contracting activity (N39430-26-D-4004).

Marine Solutions Inc., Nicholasville, Kentucky, was awarded a firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for architect-engineering services for routine inspection of waterfront facilities. Work will be performed outside the continental U.S. and is expected to be completed by August 2031. The maximum dollar value, including the base period, is $15,000,000. Fiscal 2026 Navy Working Capital funds in the amount of $10,000 will be obligated at time of award to satisfy the minimum guarantee, and funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with two offers received. Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center, Port Hueneme, California, is the contracting activity (N39430-26-D-4005).

Huntington Ingalls Inc., Ingalls Shipbuilding Division, Pascagoula, Mississippi, is awarded a cost-plus award fee $10,678,527 modification to previously awarded delivery order (N69316-25-F-6000) in support of the future USS Ted Stevens (DDG 128) post shakedown availability. Work will be performed in Mayport, Florida, and is expected to be completed by October 2027. Fiscal 2026 shipbuilding and construction (Navy) funding in the amount of $10,000,000 was obligated at the time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

Persistent Systems LLC, New York, New York, has been awarded a $104,661,109 modification (P00008) to previously awarded contract FA8214-24-C-0004 to integrate the Regional Operating Picture requirement into the Wave Relay Tactical Assault Kit contract. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $146,420,185 from $41,759,076. Work will be performed at Hill Air Force Base, Utah; F.E. Warren AFB, Wyoming; Malmstrom AFB, Montana; and Minot AFB, North Dakota, and is expected to be completed by Sept. 22, 2029. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $2,627,514 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center, Hill Air Force Base, Utah, is the contracting activity. (Awarded Aug. 7, 2026).

Skookum Educational Programs, doing business as Tessera, Bremerton, Washington, has been awarded a $70,006,743 firm-fixed-price contract for base operations maintenance services. This contract provides for operations and maintenance of infrastructure through performance work tasks, preventative maintenance, real property, and real property installed equipment inspections on building structures. Work will be performed at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska, and is expected to be completed by July 24, 2030. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $5,195,812 are being obligated at time of award. The 673rd Contracting Squadron, Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska, is the contracting activity (FA5000-26-C-0008).

Lockheed Martin Space, Littleton, Colorado, has been awarded a $22,021,262 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification (P00007) to contract FA9453-25-C-X054 for the Space Data Networking Experimentation Phase II program. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $22,461,947 from $22,021,262. Work will be performed in Littleton, Colorado, and is expected to be completed by October 2028. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $2,000,000 are being obligated, by purchase request, at the time of award. The Air Force Research Laboratory, Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico, is the contracting activity.

M.C Dean, Tysons, Virginia, was awarded a $92,424,046 firm-fixed price contract for 24/7 operations, maintenance, and repair. Nineteen bids were solicited with three received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of August 4, 2026. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Engineering and Support Center, Huntsville, Alabama, is the contracting activity (W912DY-26-F-A067).

P & S Construction Inc., Westford, Massachusetts (W912WJ-26-D-A002); Structural Associates Inc.,* East Syracuse, New York, (W912WJ-26-D-A003); H.V. Collins Co. Inc.,* Providence, Rhode Island (W912WJ-26-D-A004); and Maron Construction Co. Inc.,* Providence, Rhode Island (W912WJ-26-D-A005), will compete for each order of the $90,000,000 firm-fixed price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for design-build construction services. Bids were solicited via the internet with nine received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Aug. 10, 2031. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Concord, Massachusetts, is the contracting activity.

Genesis Systems LLC,* Tampa, Florida, was awarded a $49,898,000 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for research, development, testing, and direct procurement of the WaterCube Atmospheric Water Generation family of systems to provide scalable, on-site potable water production in austere and contested environments. One bid was solicited with one received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Aug. 10, 2031. Army Contracting Command, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland, is the contracting activity (W911QX-26-D-A004).

General Constructors Inc. of the Quad Cities, Bettendorf, Iowa, was awarded a $34,376,322 firm-fixed-price contract for demolition, temporary traffic control, clearing and grubbing, water diversion, riprap and aggregate placement, pile installation, floodwall construction, utility modifications, storm sewer installation, and site restoration. Bids were solicited via the internet with two received. Work will be performed in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, with an estimated completion date of July 10, 2028. Fiscal 2026 civil construction funds in the amount of $34,376,322 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Rock Island, Illinois, is the contracting activity (W912EK-26-C-A022).

Norfolk Dredging Co., Chesapeake, Virginia, was awarded a $27,250,950 firm-fixed price contract for maintenance dredging of the Delaware River, Philadelphia to Sea and Wilmington Harbor Project. Bids were solicited via the internet with three received. Work will be performed in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with an estimated completion date of July 13, 2027. Fiscal 2025 and 2026 civil operation and maintenance funds in the amount of $27,250,950 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity (W912BU-26-C-A032).

Sechan Electronics Inc., Lititz, Pennsylvania, was awarded a $22,119,790 cost-plus-fixed-fee, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for repair services for the Paladin Digital Fire Control System for M109A6 Self Propelled Howitzers. Bids were solicited via the internet with one received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of July 30, 2031. Army Contracting Command, Detroit Arsenal, Michigan, is the contracting activity (W912CH-26-D-0060). (Awarded July 30, 2026).

Boston Scientific Neuromodulation Corp., Valencia, California, has been awarded a maximum $14,379,072 fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for Neuromodulation procedural packages and supplies. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a five-year contract with no option periods. The ordering period end date is Aug. 16, 2031. Using customers are Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps and federal civilian agencies. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2031 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPE2DE-26-D-0008).

AVOX Systems Inc., Lancaster, New York, has been awarded a maximum $9,201,610 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-quantity contract for oxygen masks. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in the Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a two-year contract with no option periods. The ordering period end date is Aug. 9, 2028. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2028 defense working capital funds. The using military service is Navy. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support, Richmond, Virginia (SPE4A7-26-D-0269).

CORRECTION: The contract announced on July 31, 2026, for American Material Handling Inc.,* Watkinsville, Georgia (SPE8EC-26-D-0021), for $157,000,000 was announced with an incorrect award date. The correct award date is Aug. 6, 2026. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
